newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures tumble after December sets high.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures tumble after December sets high.

text.p: December CME hog futures posted a new contract high around midsession but prices tumbled late and most months finished lower as did pork belly futures, traders said.

December hogs set a new high of 59.300 cents per lb early but closed 0.225 lower at 58.225 cents. Other months ranged 0.425 cent higher to 0.350 lower with February up most on continued rolling of longs from December into that month.
Pork bellies also tumbled from early short-covering gains to finish with losses of 1.300 to 0.100 cent. February settled off 0.600 at 76.025 cents.

Values in both pits rose early on support from forecasts for continued strong cash markets. But actual cash hog prices ranged mostly steady to lower Wednesday and cash belly values were quoted lower at noon which sparked short covering and other selling, quickly pulling most months down for net losses, traders said.

Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp, said that a pickup in slaughter the past couple of days countered packer statements that they would continue to cut back on kills due to tight market supplies of hogs.

"First, the packers gave us lip service that they were going to cut back the kills this week and now we are getting statements that "we are adding hours to our kills because we're finding the hogs" so that took the strength out of the December (hog futures) contract plus also set back the bellies," Levitt said.

Strong cash pork prices and rising cutout values prompted some of the early strength in both pits. Pork cutout values late Tuesday were the highest since October 10 and closing cash bellies Tuesday were quoted at highest levels since October 8.

Expectations for Friday's USDA Cold Storage Report for frozen belly stocks also pointed to historically low levels. The average analyst estimate for stocks as of November 1 was 16.0 million lbs and compares with the average for the last 10 years of 22.8 million lbs.

But cash bellies turned easier at Wednesday's noon quote as did some other pork prices, which may result in a setback in pork product values. It is not unusual for pork prices to slip around the holiday period, traders added.
